advances: The complete original cubic-depth moment has an absolute lower bound when an arbitrary positive multiplier depends jointly on all child blocks of polynomially many full rooted spines and all coordinates in the first seven depths, and the remaining field has path variation at most one. The proof establishes the forest exit geometry, immutable-label census, actual-halfspace witnesses, and summable fourth-power class transfer directly. It does not assume a general-field entropy estimate or an all-support moment theorem.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. Accepted fact 032423921efad6c8 supplies the exact chain/tree support, unique sources, inverse reconstruction, and level census. Accepted fact 604889294a17d7df supplies the original height support and parameter bounds. Accepted fact c6487efe457e5084 fixes the reused path-variation and full Boolean-normalizer conventions. Accepted fact d9c4b095a13caaba supplies its pointwise neighbor-and-endpoint actual-halfspace selection and scalar height estimates. The forest partition and cardinalities, enlarged-label census, preservation of all witnesses, full conditional normalizers, threshold-dependent capacity sum, and exact fourth-power transfer are proved here.
proof:
We use the tree, unique Boolean source, and inverse reconstruction from accepted fact 032423921efad6c8 and the exact original columns from accepted fact 604889294a17d7df. In particular, reduction modulo two recovers the full source of a spatial point. Put
$$
\eta=2^{-m}|D_m|=1-2^{-m}\binom m{m/2},\qquad\delta=1-\eta,
\qquad T_s=\sum_{t=a_s}^{k}2^{-t}.
$$
These predecessors give
$$
Q\ge4,\qquad 0<\delta<(Q+1)^{-2},\qquad\eta^Q>\frac34,
\qquad T_s\le2\,2^{-a_s}.
\tag{1}
$$
For later counting, let
$$
\vartheta_i=2^{-m}|\lbrace c\in D_m:i_m(c)=i\rbrace|.
$$
There are exactly \(2^m\delta\) symmetric chains, and each chain adds a given coordinate at most once. Consequently
$$
0\le\vartheta_i\le\delta,\qquad\sum_i\vartheta_i=\eta.
\tag{2}
$$
In fact every \(\vartheta_i\) is positive: the chain from the empty set to the full set adds each coordinate once. This also proves (2) directly for every permitted partition, without imposing a special partition.

Here is the exact restriction rule used throughout. For a nonempty spatial class, lift it by retaining every original height of every column, and call the lifted class \(E\). Let \(\nu_E\) be the restriction of the actual measure \(\sum_{\mathbf I}w_{\mathbf I}\delta_{\mathbf I}\), let \(W_E=\nu_E(\mathbb R^N)>0\), and put \(p^E=\nu_E/W_E\). All depths of \(p^E\) use all closed halfspaces of \(\mathbb R^N\). With \(h_{\nu_E}=W_E\tau_{p^E}\),
$$
M_3(p^E)=W_E^{-4}\sum_{\mathbf I\in E}w_{\mathbf I}h_{\nu_E}(\mathbf I)^3
\ge W_E^{-4}\sum_{\mathbf I\in E}w_{\mathbf I}^4,
\tag{3}
$$
since every containing halfspace contains the atom itself. For positive \(x_1,\ldots,x_K\), Hölder gives
$$
\sum_{r=1}^{K}x_r^4\ge K^{-3}\left(\sum_{r=1}^{K}x_r\right)^4.
\tag{4}
$$
If a spatial class has a fixed level \(s\), has \(K\) points, and has spatial weight sum \(L_E=\sum_zG(z|_U)e^{\lambda\cdot z}\), then \(W_E=T_sL_E\le2\,2^{-a_s}L_E\). Keeping only its actual entrance-height atoms in (3), then using (4), gives
$$
M_3(p^E)\ge\frac1{16K^3}.
\tag{5}
$$
This bound allows arbitrary positive spatial weights.

For any finite partition into nonempty lifted classes put \(\alpha_E=W_E/W\). On a point of \(E\), every containing ambient halfspace has full mass at least \(\alpha_E\) times its conditional mass, so \(\tau_p\ge\alpha_E\tau_{p^E}\). Since the sampling mass on \(E\) is \(\alpha_Ep^E\), the exact transfer is
$$
M_3(p)\ge\sum_E\alpha_E^4M_3(p^E).
\tag{6}
$$
If \(M_3(p^E)\ge8^{-n}\kappa_E\), then another application of Hölder yields
$$
M_3(p)\ge8^{-n}\left(\sum_E\kappa_E^{-1/3}\right)^{-3}.
\tag{7}
$$
Indeed, \(1=\sum_E\alpha_E\le(\sum_E\kappa_E\alpha_E^4)^{1/4}(\sum_E\kappa_E^{-1/3})^{3/4}\). Empty spatial classes are always omitted before any conditional normalizer is defined.

If \(Q<7\), partition by all \(Q+1\le7\) spatial levels. Each level has at most \(2^n\) points by the predecessor's census. Thus (5) gives \(\kappa_E=1/16\) for each class, regardless of \(G\). Equations (6)--(7) give
$$
M_3(p)\ge\frac{8^{-n}}{16\cdot7^3}>2^{-13}8^{-n}=2^{-10}8^{-N}.
\tag{8}
$$
This already proves the assertion in this case. In particular it also covers \(U=\mathcal T_{m,Q}\) and \(\lambda=0\).

Assume henceforth \(Q\ge7\). For a spatial point of level \(s\), denote its selected prefix by \(u_1,\ldots,u_s\). Use the following spatial partition:

* Seven early classes consist of all points of levels \(0,1,\ldots,6\), respectively.
* \(\mathrm{GOOD}\) consists of points of level \(s\ge7\) with \(u_7\notin P_7\).
* For \(7\le j\le Q\), \(\mathrm{STOP}_j\) consists of level-\(j\) points with \(u_j\in P_j\).
* For \(7\le j<Q\), \(\mathrm{BRANCH}_j\) consists of points of level at least \(j+1\) with \(u_j\in P_j\) and \(u_{j+1}\notin P_{j+1}\).

The STOP condition describes the point's level and does not require its source to fail at the next block. Ancestor closure implies that if a selected node leaves the forest then none of its descendants can return. Thus a point of level at least seven either has left by its seventh selection, has its entire selected prefix in the forest, or has a unique first exit at depth \(j+1>7\). The displayed classes are therefore disjoint and exhaustive.

There are at most \(B\) nodes in every \(P_j\). For any fixed \(v\in P_j\), its root-to-\(v\) path prescribes \(j\) directions, say \(i_1,\ldots,i_j\). Disjointness of the visited child blocks and the unique-source property give exactly
$$
2^n\prod_{r=1}^{j}\vartheta_{i_r}
$$
level-\(j\) points with this selected path. No condition is imposed on unvisited blocks. Distinct \(v\)'s give disjoint sets. It follows from (2) that
$$
|\mathrm{STOP}_j|\le2^nB\delta^j.
\tag{9}
$$
Let \(\mathcal B_j\) be the level-\((j+1)\) anchors of \(\mathrm{BRANCH}_j\). For a fixed \(v\in P_j\), after the prescribed \(j\) directions the next pattern must select a child outside the set \(\lbrace i:vi\in P_{j+1}\rbrace\). Its permitted fraction is \(\sum_{i:vi\notin P_{j+1}}\vartheta_i\le\eta\le1\). Hence the same disjoint block count gives
$$
|\mathcal B_j|\le2^nB\delta^j.
\tag{10}
$$
These inequalities also cover empty classes, which have already been omitted.

The early classes have \(\kappa_E=1/16\) by (5). The same bound and (9) give
$$
M_3(p^{\widehat{\mathrm{STOP}}_j})
\ge8^{-n}\frac1{16(B\delta^j)^3}.
\tag{11}
$$
For a branch point at level \(s\ge j+1\), replace it by its level-\((j+1)\) anchor with the same full Boolean source. At each fixed \(s\) this map is injective, since parity of the anchor recovers that source. The first exit coordinate \(u_{j+1}\) may lie in \(S\): its parent \(u_j\) is in the forest. However every later selected coordinate \(u_r\), \(r\ge j+2\), is outside \(S\), because its parent is outside the forest. It also has depth greater than seven. Thus all additional spikes beyond the anchor are outside \(U\), so the anchor and branch point have exactly the same \(G\)-multiplier. Their exponential factor ratio is at most \(e^{2P_\lambda}\).

Write \(L_j^{\mathrm b}\) for the sum of actual spatial weights over \(\mathcal B_j\). There are \(Q-j\) possible branch levels, whose entrances are at least \(a_{j+1}\). Including every original height gives
$$
W_{\widehat{\mathrm{BRANCH}}_j}
\le2e^{2P_\lambda}(Q-j)2^{-a_{j+1}}L_j^{\mathrm b}.
$$
Use the actual anchor atoms at height \(a_{j+1}\) in (3), then use (4) and (10). This proves
$$
M_3(p^{\widehat{\mathrm{BRANCH}}_j})
\ge8^{-n}\frac{e^{-8}}{16(B\delta^j)^3(Q-j)^4}.
\tag{12}
$$
No multiplier comparison between different labels is present in this estimate.

It remains to control the single class \(\mathrm{GOOD}\), if nonempty. Let
$$
\mathcal L=\lbrace z|_U:z\in\mathrm{GOOD},\ \operatorname{level}(z)=7\rbrace.
$$
All coordinates of depths at most seven belong to \(U\), so their source bits determine the first seven tests and selected nodes. Once \(u_7\notin P_7\), every later selected coordinate is outside \(S\) by ancestor closure, and has depth greater than seven. Thus it is outside \(U\). Every GOOD point has exactly the same \(U\)-label as its level-seven anchor.

Conversely, every \(\omega\in\mathcal L\) occurs at level seven with every Boolean assignment outside \(U\). Its first seven tests depend only on the fixed source bits in \(U\), and all seven spikes lie in \(U\); the remaining \(U\)-coordinates are unchanged Boolean source bits. Parity recovers the source restriction to \(U\) from \(\omega\). This restriction determines the seven selected nodes and hence the entire level-seven label. The parity map on \(\mathcal L\) is therefore injective, and
$$
0<|\mathcal L|\le2^{n_U}.
\tag{13}
$$
In particular these conclusions are about the full forest label, including the possible first exit spike in \(S\).

For every field \(\theta\) vanishing on \(U\), define
$$
Z_\theta^{\mathrm{out}}=\prod_{u\notin U}(1+e^{\theta_u}),
\qquad
Z_\theta=\prod_{u\in\mathcal T_{m,Q}}(1+e^{\theta_u})
=2^{n_U}Z_\theta^{\mathrm{out}}.
\tag{14}
$$
Thus \(Z_\theta\) is the full Boolean normalizer in the convention of accepted fact c6487efe457e5084, and (14) is its explicit map to the outside normalizer used here. An empty outside product equals one. Put
$$
\mathfrak g_1=\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal L}G(\omega),
\qquad\mathfrak g_4=\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal L}G(\omega)^4.
$$
Equation (4), (13), and \((1+x)^4\le8(1+x^4)\) give
$$
\frac{\mathfrak g_4}{\mathfrak g_1^4}\ge8^{-n_U},
\qquad
\frac{Z_{4\lambda}^{\mathrm{out}}}{(Z_\lambda^{\mathrm{out}})^4}
\ge8^{-(n-n_U)}.
\tag{15}
$$
The second inequality is multiplied over exactly the coordinates outside \(U\).

At every fixed level \(s\ge7\) and fixed label \(\omega\), the source map injects its GOOD points into all Boolean assignments outside \(U\). The seven initial spikes have zero field, and the remaining spikes multiply the Boolean field weight by at most \(e^{2P_\lambda}\). Dropping only the forward-success restrictions and summing every original height gives
$$
W_{\widehat{\mathrm{GOOD}}}
\le e^{2P_\lambda}\mathfrak g_1Z_\lambda^{\mathrm{out}}R_k,
\qquad
R_k:=\sum_{s=0}^{Q}T_s
\le2+2\sum_{\ell=8}^{k}b_\ell2^{-\ell}
\le2+\frac{H_k-H_7}{4}
\le\frac{9+\log k}{4}.
\tag{16}
$$
Here \(H_j=\sum_{r=1}^{j}1/r\), and \(H_k\le1+\log k\). This is a bound on the full GOOD conditional normalizer, not a global density comparison.

For \(7\le s\le Q\) and \(\omega\in\mathcal L\), let \(\mathcal C_s(\omega)\) consist of its GOOD level-\(s\) points whose canonical inverse reconstruction reaches depth \(Q\). For every field \(\theta\) zero on \(U\), we claim
$$
\sum_{z\in\mathcal C_s(\omega)}e^{\theta\cdot z}
\ge\eta^{Q-7}e^{-3\Pi(\theta)}Z_\theta^{\mathrm{out}}.
\tag{17}
$$
To prove this, fix the source restriction to \(U\) and its first seven selected nodes, as recovered from \(\omega\). Give every outside coordinate an independent Boolean bit with probability proportional to \(e^{\theta_u b_u}\), with product normalizer \(Z_\theta^{\mathrm{out}}\). Starting at the seventh selected node, require \(s-7\) forward tests in \(D_m\), followed by \(Q-s\) inverse tests in \(\operatorname{im}F_m\). In an inverse test the Boolean block is a prospective center block, and its unique predecessor under \(F_m\) chooses the next node. All \(Q-7\) tested blocks are fresh and disjoint, and they lie outside \(U\): their parent nodes are descendants of \(u_7\), which is outside the forest, and their coordinate depths exceed seven.

Under fair outside bits, each successive test has conditional success probability \(\eta\), so the total success probability is exactly \(\eta^{Q-7}\). A successful transcript fixes just the patterns of these adaptively visited blocks. Its cylinder leaves all other outside bits free. Two different transcripts give disjoint cylinders, since their first different pattern is tested at the same location determined by their common earlier patterns. For a revealed bit \(b_u\), the ratio of its product-law probability to its fair probability is
$$
\frac{2e^{\theta_ub_u}}{1+e^{\theta_u}}\ge e^{-|\theta_u|}.
$$
The revealed blocks lie on one full rooted path. The probability ratio of each successful cylinder is therefore at least \(e^{-\Pi(\theta)}\); unexposed bits integrate to one. Summing the disjoint cylinders bounds the product-law success probability below by \(e^{-\Pi(\theta)}\eta^{Q-7}\).

On success, form a spatial point by changing the selected zero to two in the first \(s\) forward blocks, including the seven fixed initial blocks. Leave the inverse-tested Boolean blocks unchanged. The resulting point is in \(\mathcal C_s(\omega)\): its forward prefix has length \(s\), and the remaining center blocks have the prescribed inverse continuation. This map is a bijection onto \(\mathcal C_s(\omega)\). Parity recovers the source, the first \(s\) forward blocks recover the prefix, and injectivity of \(F_m\) recovers the inverse suffix, including its locations and patterns. At \(s=7\) or \(s=Q\), the corresponding empty part requires no test. The field factor introduced by the forward spikes is at least \(e^{-2\Pi(\theta)}\); the seven initial spikes have zero field. Multiplication by this factor and \(Z_\theta^{\mathrm{out}}\) proves (17).

First let \(k\ge2^{16}\), and put \(L=\log k\) and \(g=\lfloor\sqrt{k}\rfloor\). The scalar estimates in accepted fact d9c4b095a13caaba give
$$
L>9,\qquad
\sum_{\ell=8}^{g}b_\ell2^{-\ell}\ge\frac L{32},
\qquad R_k\le\frac L2.
$$
Every \(a_s\) with \(s\ge1\) is at least eight. Deleting just the first six positive spatial levels therefore gives
$$
U_{\ge7}:=\sum_{\substack{7\le s\le Q\\a_s\le g}}2^{-a_s}
\ge\frac L{32}-\frac6{256}\ge\frac L{64}.
\tag{18}
$$
The last inequality follows already from \(L>9\). Use only the actual sampling points
$$
\mathcal G_U=\left\lbrace(z,a_s+1):
 z\in\mathcal C_s(\omega),\ \omega\in\mathcal L,
 \quad s\ge7,\quad a_s\le g\right\rbrace.
$$
These heights lie in their original columns because \(a_s+1\le g+1\le k\).

Fix such a point. Let \(u_{s+1},\ldots,u_Q\) be its inverse continuation, and put \(V_r=\sum_{q=s+1}^{r}e_{u_q}\). The pointwise actual-halfspace argument of accepted fact d9c4b095a13caaba proves that every closed ambient halfspace containing \((z,a_s+1)\) contains distinct original indices of total untilted weight at least \(L/128\), chosen solely from
$$
(z-e_{u_r},a_s),\qquad(z-V_r,a_r),\qquad(z+V_r,a_r),\qquad r>s.
\tag{19}
$$
This is the same original geometry and entrance sequence as in that fact. To specify the pointwise input precisely, for a halfspace through the sample with nonnegative height coefficient, at least one reconstructed endpoint is included for every \(a_r\ge2g\), whose total untilted weight is at least \(L/32\). For negative height coefficient \(-\beta\), a lower neighbor is included whenever the corresponding spatial coefficient \(c_{u_r}\le\beta\). Either these neighbors already give \(L/128\), or there are fewer than \(2^{a_s}L/128\) such indices. Between them, the normalized endpoint partial sums have increments greater than one, so at most \(4k2^gL\) partial sums lie in \([-k,k]\). Deleting these endpoint indices loses at most \(4k2^{-g}L\le L/64\), since \(2^g\ge256k\). The remaining endpoints yield at least \(L/64\). These are exactly the scalar and distinctness estimates established in d9c4b095a13caaba. Every containing proper halfspace contains a parallel one through the sample, and the whole-space case is immediate.

All points in (19) are still GOOD and have exactly the same \(U\)-label \(\omega\). Indeed, every modified coordinate has depth greater than \(s\ge7\) on a descendant path of \(u_7\notin P_7\); hence it lies outside \(S\) and outside the first seven coordinate depths. The first seven selections remain unchanged. Inverse reconstruction gives the endpoint levels \(s,r\), and the lower neighbors have level \(s\) because changing a suffix one to zero leaves the first \(s\) forward blocks intact. Thus each displayed height is an original permissible height, and none of the selected mass leaves the conditional class. Every displayed displacement changes coordinates of one full path by at most one in absolute value, so its field weight is at least \(e^{\lambda\cdot z-P_\lambda}\). Multipliers are exactly equal, not estimated. Consequently
$$
h_{\nu_{\widehat{\mathrm{GOOD}}}}(z,a_s+1)
\ge G(\omega)e^{\lambda\cdot z-P_\lambda}\frac L{128}.
\tag{20}
$$
This holds for every original containing closed ambient halfspace, including directions constant on a label slice.

Sum the cube of (20) against the actual GOOD atom weights, retaining the fourth power of its full normalizer. Apply (17) with \(\theta=4\lambda\), so \(\Pi(4\lambda)=4P_\lambda\), then use (1), (15), (16), and (18). We obtain
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_3(p^{\widehat{\mathrm{GOOD}}})
&\ge\frac{e^{-3P_\lambda}L^3}{128^3W_{\widehat{\mathrm{GOOD}}}^4}
\sum_{\substack{s\ge7\\a_s\le g}}2^{-(a_s+1)}
\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal L}G(\omega)^4
\sum_{z\in\mathcal C_s(\omega)}e^{4\lambda\cdot z}\\
&\ge\frac{\eta^{Q-7}e^{-15P_\lambda}
 \mathfrak g_4Z_{4\lambda}^{\mathrm{out}}U_{\ge7}L^3}
 {2\cdot128^3W_{\widehat{\mathrm{GOOD}}}^4}\\
&\ge3\cdot2^{-26}e^{-23P_\lambda}
 \frac{\mathfrak g_4}{\mathfrak g_1^4}
 \frac{Z_{4\lambda}^{\mathrm{out}}}{(Z_\lambda^{\mathrm{out}})^4}\\
&\ge3\cdot2^{-26}e^{-23}8^{-n}>2^{-84}8^{-n}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{21}
$$
Here the exponential cost is twelve from the fourth-field census, three from the cubed depth, and eight from the fourth normalizer. For the last generous numerical bound, \(e^{23}<3^{23}<2^{37}\), since \(3^5<2^8\) and \(3^3<2^5\).

Now let \(8\le k<2^{16}\). Equation (16) gives \(R_k<8\). Since \(Q\ge7\), the level-seven entrance exists and satisfies \(a_7\le14\). One direct check is \(b_8=4\) and \(b_9=7\): thus \(Q\ge7\) forces \(k\ge9\), and in fact \(a_7=9\le14\). In particular it is not necessary, or correct, to assign entrance eight to level seven. Every \(\omega\in\mathcal L\) occurs at level seven with every Boolean assignment outside \(U\). Its seven spikes have zero field. The exact sum of fourth powers of the actual entrance atom weights is therefore
$$
2^{-4a_7}\mathfrak g_4Z_{4\lambda}^{\mathrm{out}}
\ge2^{-56}\mathfrak g_4Z_{4\lambda}^{\mathrm{out}}.
$$
Equations (3), (15), and (16) imply
$$
M_3(p^{\widehat{\mathrm{GOOD}}})
>2^{-68}e^{-8P_\lambda}
\frac{\mathfrak g_4}{\mathfrak g_1^4}
\frac{Z_{4\lambda}^{\mathrm{out}}}{(Z_\lambda^{\mathrm{out}})^4}
\ge2^{-68}e^{-8}8^{-n}>2^{-84}8^{-n},
\tag{22}
$$
using \(e^8<3^8<2^{13}\). This argument also includes a single-height anchor column. Thus whenever GOOD is nonempty it has the uniform choice \(\kappa_{\widehat{\mathrm{GOOD}}}=2^{-84}\).

It remains to sum the capacities in (7). Equations (5), (11), (12), (21), and (22) allow
$$
\begin{aligned}
\kappa_{\mathrm{early},s}&=1/16 &&(0\le s\le6),\\
\kappa_{\widehat{\mathrm{STOP}}_j}&=\frac1{16(B\delta^j)^3}&&(7\le j\le Q),\\
\kappa_{\widehat{\mathrm{BRANCH}}_j}
&=\frac{e^{-8}}{16(B\delta^j)^3(Q-j)^4}&&(7\le j<Q),\\
\kappa_{\widehat{\mathrm{GOOD}}}&=2^{-84}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Only nonempty classes enter this list. The early contribution is less than \(21\), and the GOOD contribution, if present, is \(2^{28}\). Since \(Q\ge7\), one has \(\delta<1/64\), and the assumed forest threshold gives
$$
B\delta^7\le64(Q+1)^{-3}\le64,
\qquad
BQ^{4/3}\delta^7
\le64\frac{Q^{4/3}}{(Q+1)^3}
\le64(Q+1)^{-5/3}\le64.
\tag{23}
$$
Using \(16^{1/3}<3\), \(e^{8/3}<27\), and \((1-\delta)^{-1}<2\), we get the absolute bounds
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{j=7}^{Q}\kappa_{\widehat{\mathrm{STOP}}_j}^{-1/3}
&\le16^{1/3}\frac{B\delta^7}{1-\delta}<384,\\
\sum_{j=7}^{Q-1}\kappa_{\widehat{\mathrm{BRANCH}}_j}^{-1/3}
&\le16^{1/3}e^{8/3}\frac{BQ^{4/3}\delta^7}{1-\delta}<10368.
\end{aligned}
\tag{24}
$$
In particular the threshold \(B\le64(Q+1)^{11}\) has been used quantitatively, rather than replacing the forest by a depth-dependent number of unrestricted classes. The seven early levels were kept as seven classes throughout.

The total capacity is less than
$$
2^{28}+21+384+10368<2^{29}.
$$
Equation (7) now yields
$$
M_3(p)>2^{-87}8^{-n}=2^{-84}8^{-N}\ge2^{-200}8^{-N}.
$$
Together with (8), this proves the theorem for every \(k\ge8\). Every lifted class kept all original column heights in its denominator, and the exhaustive partition and fourth-power transfer use exactly the full original \(W\) and \(p\). Every witness and every depth comparison used all original ambient closed halfspaces. No all-support entropy premise or global density ratio was used.
statement:
Fix an integer \(k\ge8\), and use exactly the \(\rho_t=2^{-t}\) specialization of accepted fact 604889294a17d7df with the rooted tree of accepted fact 032423921efad6c8. Explicitly, put
$$
b_\ell=0\quad(1\le\ell<8),\qquad
b_\ell=\left\lfloor\frac{2^\ell}{8\ell}\right\rfloor\quad(8\le\ell\le k),
\qquad Q_0=0,\quad Q_\ell=\sum_{r=1}^{\ell}b_r,\quad Q=Q_k,
$$
$$
m=2(Q+1)^4,\qquad n=\sum_{r=1}^{Q}m^r,\qquad N=n+1.
$$
The height cutoff is \(k\), the tree depth is \(Q\), and the spatial dimension is \(n\). Set \(a_0=0\) and \(a_s=\ell\) when \(Q_{\ell-1}<s\le Q_\ell\).

Choose any symmetric saturated chain partition of \(\lbrace0,1\rbrace^m\), with its nonterminal set \(D_m\) and injective successor
\(F_m(c)=c+e_{i_m(c)}\), where \(c_{i_m(c)}=0\). The coordinate tree is
$$
\mathcal T_{m,Q}=\bigcup_{r=1}^{Q}\lbrace1,\ldots,m\rbrace^r.
$$
For a node \(v\) of depth less than \(Q\), including the empty root, its child block is \(z[v]=(z_{v1},\ldots,z_{vm})\). For a Boolean source \(b\), start at the root and continue from \(v\) to \(vi_m(b[v])\) while \(b[v]\in D_m\), stopping at the first failure or at depth \(Q\). Let the resulting length be \(h(b)\), with selected nodes \(u_1,\ldots,u_{h(b)}\). Retain the complete original supports
$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{m,Q}
&=\left\lbrace z_s(b)=b+2\sum_{r=1}^{s}e_{u_r}:
 b\in\lbrace0,1\rbrace^{\mathcal T_{m,Q}},\ 0\le s\le h(b)\right\rbrace,\\
\widehat A
&=\left\lbrace(z,t):z\in A_{m,Q},\quad
 a_{\operatorname{level}(z)}\le t\le k,\quad t\in\mathbb Z\right\rbrace.
\end{aligned}
$$
Here level is the number of coordinates equal to two, as in the predecessors.

Let a nonempty family of \(B\) full rooted paths of length \(Q\) be given, where
$$
1\le B\le64(Q+1)^{11}.
$$
For \(0\le j\le Q\), let \(P_j\) be the set of their depth-\(j\) nodes. Thus \(P_0=\lbrace\varnothing\rbrace\), and their union is ancestor-closed. Define the coordinate sets
$$
S=\bigcup_{j=0}^{Q-1}\ \bigcup_{v\in P_j}\lbrace vi:1\le i\le m\rbrace,
\qquad
U=S\cup\lbrace u\in\mathcal T_{m,Q}:|u|\le\min(7,Q)\rbrace,
\qquad n_U=|U|.
$$
The node sets \(P_j\) and the coordinate set \(S\) have different meanings: in particular, a child outside \(P_{j+1}\) still lies in \(S\) if its parent belongs to \(P_j\).

Let \(G:R_U\to(0,\infty)\) be arbitrary, where \(R_U=\lbrace z|_U:z\in A_{m,Q}\rbrace\). Let \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^n\) vanish on \(U\), and suppose
$$
P_\lambda:=\Pi(\lambda)
=\max_{v_0,\ldots,v_Q}
\sum_{j=0}^{Q-1}\sum_{i=1}^{m}|\lambda_{v_ji}|\le1,
$$
where the maximum ranges over full rooted paths. This is exactly the path-variation normalization used in accepted fact c6487efe457e5084; no rescaling of its field or of its Boolean normalizer is made.

At every original index put
$$
w_{(z,t)}=G(z|_U)e^{\lambda\cdot z}2^{-t},
\qquad W=\sum_{\mathbf I\in\widehat A}w_{\mathbf I},
\qquad p_{\mathbf I}=w_{\mathbf I}/W,
$$
and put zero weights off \(\widehat A\). Define
$$
\tau_p(\mathbf I)=\inf\left\lbrace p(H):
 H\subseteq\mathbb R^N\text{ is a closed halfspace containing }\mathbf I\right\rbrace,
\qquad M_3(p)=\sum_{\mathbf I\in\widehat A}p_{\mathbf I}\tau_p(\mathbf I)^3.
$$
Then
$$
M_3(p)\ge2^{-200}8^{-N}.
$$
This concerns every original spatial point, every original height in each column, the full original \(W\) and sampling law, and all containing closed halfspaces of the original ambient space. The coefficient is independent of \(k,Q,B\), the chain partition, the forest, \(G\), and \(\lambda\).
